questions.q_en: Which of the following was NOT a factor contributing to the rise of Extremism in the Indian National Congress?
options_en: The failure of the Moderates' methods
The impact of social reform movements
The establishment of the Indian National Congress in 1885
The imperialist policies of Lord Curzon
questions.solution_en:
• The INC was formed in 1885 as a platform for political discussion but did not immediately lead to extremism.

• The Extremists emerged due to dissatisfaction with the Moderates' policies, influence of social reformers, and British repression.

• Lord Curzon's policies like the Partition of Bengal fueled extremist sentiments.

questions.q_en: What was the main ideological difference between the Moderates and the Extremists?
options_en: Moderates relied on petitions, while Extremists advocated active resistance
Moderates opposed British rule, while Extremists supported it
Moderates encouraged violence, while Extremists followed a peaceful approach
Extremists wanted dominion status, while Moderates sought complete independence
questions.solution_en:
• The Moderates believed in constitutional methods like petitions, prayer and discussions.

• The Extremists, led by leaders like Tilak, Pal, and Lajpat Rai, believed in self-reliance, boycotts, and direct action.

• Both sought Swaraj, but Extremists wanted immediate self-rule, while Moderates aimed for gradual reforms.

• Features of the Extremist Faction:

○ Rejected constitutional methods and emphasized aggressive resistance.

○ Advocated Swadeshi, Boycott, and National Education.

○ Opposed British partition of Bengal (1905).

○ Criticized the Moderates for their petition-based politics.

○ Influenced by radical nationalism and self-rule (Swaraj) demand.

questions.q_en: The immediate cause of the split between Moderates and Extremists in the INC was:
options_en: Differences over the approach towards social reform
The method of resistance against the Partition of Bengal
Personal rivalry between Tilak and Gokhale
The issue of Swaraj as the ultimate goal of INC
questions.solution_en:
• The split occurred at the Surat Session (1907) due to differing approaches in method of resistance against the Partition of Bengal.

• Moderates favored petitions, while Extremists wanted agitation and boycott movements.

• Though ideological differences existed before, the Partition of Bengal intensified the conflict.

• Surat Split (1907)

○ It marked the division between Moderates and Extremists due to ideological differences.

○ Moderates (led by Gopal Krishna Gokhale) preferred gradual reforms and working with the British.

○ Extremists (led by Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai, and Bipin Chandra Pal) demanded Swaraj and direct action.

○ The split happened over the selection of the INC President - Moderates supported Rash Behari Ghosh, while Extremists wanted Tilak.

○ The session turned violent, and Tilak's supporters were forcefully expelled.

questions.q_en: What was the main objective of the Swadeshi Movement?
options_en: To create a separate electorate for Indians
questions.solution_en:
• The Swadeshi Movement aimed to reduce dependence on British goods.

• It was a response to the Partition of Bengal and promoted economic self-reliance.

• Swadeshi Movement (1905-1911)

○ Launched in 1905 as a response to Lord Curzon's partition of Bengal.

○ Swadeshi" means 'of one's own country', promoting self-reliance and indigenous goods.

○ Prominent leaders included Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai, Bipin Chandra Pal, Aurobindo Ghosh, and Rabindranath Tagore.

○ Focused on boycotting British goods like textiles and promoting Indian-made products.

questions.q_en: Which of the following was NOT a method used by the Extremists?
questions.solution_en:
• The Extremists rejected constitutional methods, which were favored by Moderates.

• Boycott of foreign goods, Swadeshi movement, and Passive resistance were key strategies used by the Extremists to oppose British rule.

• Swadeshi and Boycott - Advocated the use of Indian-made goods and rejection of British products.

• Passive Resistance - Encouraged non-cooperation with British authorities, including refusing to pay taxes and resigning from government jobs.

• Public Meetings & Propaganda - Conducted speeches, processions, and distributed leaflets to spread nationalist ideas.
